verdict.reasoning: Patient states: "been having some problems with my hearing" and "notice that my face has been feeling a bit numb recently," indicating hearing problems and facial numbness as the main issues.
Doctor says: "It's been a few weeks now. About three weeks or something" and clarifies it is on the left side: "Just on my left side. I've noticed that the hearing's kind of gone down a bit."
Doctor describes: "it's the left side. It's kind of like around my left ear and kind of along here. So like my jawline sort of feeling a bit numb around here."
Patient mentions "Occasionally notice" and clinician completes "Some ringing in your ear," which is accepted, indicating occasional tinnitus.
Patient states: "especially sometimes when I get a ringing, I feel a bit dizzy" and repeats: "like the ringing occasionally and when I get back and sometimes feel a bit dizzy."
Patient says: "I've got kind of been told I had polyps in my nose in the past."
Patient reports: "I think they said ages ago I had something called can't quite remember, but labyrinthitis, something like that."
Patient notes: "if my polyps are playing up, I've got a spray" and later: "I only take the spray for my nose when I need it" and cannot recall the name, i.e., an unknown nasal spray used as needed.
Patient says: "occasionally get some kind of hearty feeling... I take a Rennie's if I need to" and "sometimes take over like Rennie, but I just get that from the chemist," indicating PRN use.
In response to allergy query, doctor says: "No, just latex," indicating a latex allergy.
Patient states: "My brother had neurofibromatosis. I think it is."
Patient answers: "Yeah, so I'm a jockey."
To question about living situation, patient replies: "I live with my partner."
When asked about pets: "Do you have any pets at all at home?" patient answers: "No pets."

This is a video consultation and there is no mention of any physical exam findings; clinician notes the limitation: "Obviously we're limited in terms of assessment via video portal," supporting that no in-person physical exam was done.

The discussion and plan are based on "problems with my hearing" on the left and "my face has been feeling a bit numb" on the left, i.e., unilateral hearing loss and facial numbness as key issues in the assessment.
Clinician states: "What you're describing might be something called Bell's palsy."
Clinician says they want "a neurological examination just to make sure there's nothing else going on," implying need to rule out serious neurological conditions.
Clinician: "ask them to book you in for a face to face appointment in one of our clinics within central London."
Clinician plans "a neurological examination just to make sure there's nothing else going on, confirm that that might be the diagnosis," referring to Bell's palsy.
Clinician includes in plan: "have a look inside the ear, see if there's anything to see within the ear."

Clinician says: "someone will see you and hopefully we'll be able to reassure you further" and emphasizes examination to "definitively reassure you," indicating reassurance and further evaluation based on findings.
